title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
why: Keeps the language-model backbone fixed and moves workflow definition, state, and domain knowledge into versioned control assets outside the model. Assets are updated only after a regression check and human approval, then enforced at runtime by a state machine and machine-checkable acceptance gates, with an independent auditor grading the trace. This is retained harness-level improvement of non-weight control assets on long-horizon business workflows.
mechanism: Externalized, versioned control assets (workflow, state, domain knowledge) enforced by a state machine and acceptance gates during execution; an independent auditor grades the resulting trace; assets change only after a regression check plus human approval.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated on three deployed workflows exceeding 200 steps. On Domain A, a 120-case end-to-end set shows unattended completion rising from 50% to 100%, retrieval recall from 56% to 91.67%, end-to-end latency from 440 to 159 minutes, and scenario-analysis recall from 45% to 93%. Two other domains were taken over by teams that did not write the assets, in four and seven days. A controlled ablation is reported to separate the two named failure sources (error accumulation vs vocabulary mismatch).

title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
why: Treats the agentic-RL harness itself as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains, rather than a fixed handwritten scaffold. Even though the setting is agentic RL, the central object is the non-weight harness (Compression and Steering programs over typed interaction State).
mechanism: Interaction is recorded as structured State (typed blocks). A Compression program assembles accumulated history into model context and a Steering program supplies guidance when behavior deviates. During RL training, candidate programs are proposed from recent trajectories, verified by execution, and replayed over past trajectories so the harness tracks shifts in model behavior.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): CodeSearch is studied in depth, with further analysis on ALFWorld and BIRD SQL, using models from 1.5B to 8B. The proposed Compression and Steering mechanisms improve held-out performance over the fixed-harness baseline in most settings.

title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery
why: Autonomous research agent for discovering domain-specific forecasting models that retains a hierarchical experience memory: it links mined literature to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons that are reused across later forecasting tasks. The retained object is this experience/playbook memory, not only the discovered model weights.
mechanism: Expert-inspired dual-loop workflow: hypothesis-driven architecture exploration coupled with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization from experimental feedback. The agent mines scientific literature and extracts mechanisms, evidence, and applicability conditions. A hierarchical experience memory links those findings to outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons to guide later discovery and training.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and are reported to support the dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. The abstract states that code is available but gives no URL (placeholder 'this https URL').

title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
why: Case-study audit of one shipped, untuned finance agent that locates failures in harness layers (instructions and tools vs the model) and then runs an optimization loop: it reads traces, makes one targeted change per round, and keeps the change only if it clears a fixed threshold. This is an audit plus retained instruction/tool edits, with a pre-registered rule for judging gains against run-to-run noise.
mechanism: Leave the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2 reference agent untuned. Measure score stability across repeated runs; classify failed trajectories by the layer whose owner would fix them (instructions, tools, model, data) under a taxonomy frozen in advance; then an optimization loop proposes one targeted change per round and retains it only if a fixed threshold is met, under separate cost and accuracy objectives.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): seven identical runs on 18 questions pass between 105 and 123 of 149 rubric criteria, with the bill varying by up to 17%. Of 20 failed trajectories (three runs of nine held-out questions), 13 are attributed to instructions, 3 to tools, 4 to the model, and none to data. Four blind readers name the same fault as the LLM analyzer in 94% of cases (inter-reader agreement 93%). Under a cost objective the final configuration costs 0.34x the baseline on the held-out questions (95% CI [0.22, 0.58]) at accuracy within noise; under an accuracy objective it gains 14 points on development questions and 1.5 on held-out ones (CI [-5.3, +7.2]). Against a pre-written noise rule, the authors call the cost saving real and the accuracy gain not. Framed as a case study of one agent and nine test questions, not a general result.

title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents
why: After a verifiable agentic-search formulation for powder XRD, the paper extends to experimental multiphase patterns with a reflexive evolution framework: an evolver diagnoses solver failures on self-generated synthetic problems and develops persistent guidance and executable tools that are then given to agents on measured patterns. The retained objects are those tools and guidance, not model-weight training.
mechanism: pXRD structure determination is framed as verifiable agentic search (profile agreement at inference; structural matching at evaluation). A reflexive evolution loop uses known generating structures and measurement parameters on synthetic problems so an evolver can diagnose solver failures and write persistent guidance and executable tools; that package is then supplied to agents on measured patterns. A replaceable laboratory specification defines the sample family and measurement conditions.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on pXRD-Bench (200 simulated single-phase problems), agent adaptation raises selected structural recovery from 27% to 69%, with further gains from repeated sampling and verifier-guided inference-time scaling. On 15 measured patterns from solid-state synthesis, the evolved package improves average profile agreement and transfers an analogue-substitution procedure that recovers a phase whose structure is absent from the supplied reference library.

title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
why: Across generations, human-approved construction traces are distilled into asset-ID-free Layout skills and semantic Content skills that can be retrieved and recombined, and the skill library is preserved when the system is deployed in a second game engine. This is skill-library learning from traces with retained reuse, not a one-shot scene generator.
mechanism: A canonical SceneContext holds the evolving world; backend adapters isolate engine conventions. Structured handoffs let fresh Builder sessions query this persistent state. Across generations, human-approved traces are distilled into Layout skills and Content skills that are retrieved and recombined. Deployment in a second engine keeps the shared construction protocol and skill library while replacing backend integration.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): GameSceneBench has 69 indoor and outdoor prompts. Under a common asset and evaluation protocol, SceneAgent obtains human tie-adjusted preference scores of 78.2-89.4% against five baselines. Ablations attribute gains in prompt alignment and scene completeness primarily to reusable skills and the multi-agent protocol, with additional runtime.

title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
why: v2 is a method/experiment revision of the already-ingested harness self-improvement study on ARC-AGI-3. The abs now reports that no revision retains its parent, and that a post hoc rule selecting among existing snapshots by development score raises the held-out gain to 4.53 points ([0.81, 8.68]), separating generation of revisions from the decision to deploy them. Listing comments: 'v2: revised version with additional analyses'.
mechanism: Core protocol unchanged from corpus v1: through a fixed coding bootstrap, each model constructs a task harness, acts on five development games, revises the codebase twice, and is evaluated on 20 games that never influence adaptation, using held-out RHAE and dollar inference cost. v2 adds the snapshot-selection analysis (generation of revisions vs the decision to deploy them) and notes that no revision retains its parent.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abs): across 27 lineages, two revisions raise mean held-out RHAE by only 2.80 points (95% interval [-1.44, 7.35]). No revision retains its parent, yet a post hoc rule that selects among existing snapshots by development score raises the held-out gain to 4.53 points ([0.81, 8.68]). The 2.80-point result was already in the corpus v1 abstract; the no-retain-parent finding and the 4.53-point selection rule are new in v2.
